instruction: Create a trend chart similar to the one shown in the image, using the data in the spreadsheet. Make it editable, not an image.

dim1: The delivered file is in .xlsx or .xlsm format and opens normally.
The delivered workbook retains the data worksheet used for charting, and the data range remains editable cells.
The new chart in the delivered workbook can continue to be edited using Excel's “Chart Design,” “Select Data,” “Format Data Series,” “Format Axis,” and “Format Data Labels” features.
dim2: +1: Trend chart object: It is located in the sheet1 worksheet containing the regional product sales amount data. The chart's upper-left corner is in a blank area to the right of or below the data range, at least 1 column or 2 rows away from the boundary of the data range. The chart is an Excel-editable 3-D column chart object, not an image object.

+1: Trend chart data source: The chart data comes from the cell range of the regional product sales amount table in the sheet1 workbook. The horizontal categories use sales region data, the series use year data, and the values use the corresponding sales amount data. The number of chart data series matches the number of year columns in the sheet1 table, and the number of data points matches the number of sales regions in sheet1.

+1: Trend chart type: The chart type is a 3-D clustered column chart or 3-D column chart, with columns that have three-dimensional depth and a perspective angle. Columns for different years are grouped by sales region, with the columns for multiple years displayed side by side within the same region. It must not be an ordinary 2-D column chart, line chart, pie chart, or screenshot.

+1: White trend chart area: The chart area background is white or has no fill, and the chart border has no outline or a thin light-gray outline. The chart area has no dark shading, image background, watermark, or unrelated large color block.

+1: Trend chart plot area: The plot area is in the middle of the chart, occupying 75%–90% of the chart width and 65%–82% of the chart height. The plot area background is white or very light gray, with light-gray 3-D gridlines and a rear perspective grid plane inside it.

+1: Trend chart title text at the top: It is centered at the top of the chart, with the text “Regional Shipment Volume Trend Chart.” The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimHei, or DengXian; the font size is 16 pt–20 pt; it is bold and dark blue; and the title does not overlap the plot area.

+1: Trend chart vertical-axis title text on the left: It is positioned in the middle on the left side of the chart, with the text “Shipment Volume (Ten Thousand Yuan).” The text is arranged vertically or rotated 90 degrees. The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimHei, or Calibri; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; and the color is dark blue or black.

+1: Trend chart horizontal-axis title text at the bottom: It is centered at the bottom of the chart, with the text “Sales Region.” The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimHei, or Calibri; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; it is bold or semibold; and the color is dark blue or black.

+1: Trend chart depth-axis title text on the right: It is positioned in the lower-middle portion on the right side of the chart, with the text “Year.” The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimHei, or Calibri; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; it is bold or semibold; and the color is dark blue or black.

+1: Trend chart sales-region category labels: The horizontal-axis category labels display the sales region names from the sheet1 table from left to right and should include “North China,” “South China,” “Central and Western China,” and “Western China.” The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, or Calibri; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; the color is dark blue or black; and the labels do not overlap one another.

+1: Trend chart year series labels: The depth axis or legend displays the year series from the sheet1 table and should include “2020,” “2021,” and “2022,” with a font size of 8 pt–12 pt. The year order from front to back or from left to right matches the order in the sheet1 table.

+1: Trend chart vertical-axis tick labels: The vertical-axis scale starts at 0, and its maximum scale covers the highest sales amount in the sheet1 table. The vertical-axis maximum scale should be around 10000. The tick labels “0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, 10000” are black or dark blue, with a font size of 8 pt–12 pt.

+1: Trend chart vertical-axis major gridlines: Light-gray horizontal gridlines or 3-D perspective gridlines appear in the plot area. The lines are light-gray single solid lines with a line width of 0.5 pt–1 pt, and the gridlines do not obscure the columns or data labels.

+5: 2020 column series: It corresponds to the sales amount data in the sheet1 table for 2020, and the columns have a 3-D effect. Within the same sales region, the 2021 column is in a consistent position toward the front or back of the group, and the number of data points matches the number of sales regions.

+5: 2021 column series: It corresponds to the sales amount data in the sheet1 table for 2021, and the columns have a 3-D effect. Within the same sales region, the 2021 column is in a consistent position toward the front or back of the group, and the number of data points matches the number of sales regions.

+5: 2022 column series: It corresponds to the sales amount data in the sheet1 table for 2022, and the columns have a 3-D effect. Within the same sales region, the 2022 column is in a consistent position toward the front or back of the group, and the number of data points matches the number of sales regions.
+3: The 2020, 2021, and 2022 column series use three different fill colors.

+3: Trend chart data labels: A corresponding sales amount value label appears at the top of or above each column, and each label's value matches the corresponding cell in the sheet1 table. The font is Microsoft YaHei, Calibri, or SimSun; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; the color is similar to that of the corresponding column series or is a dark color; and the labels do not extend beyond the chart area. Each label's color matches the color of the corresponding column below it.

+1: Trend chart legend at the bottom: It is located at the bottom of the chart or in a blank area at the lower right. The legend contains the three series names 2020, 2021, and 2022. The three legend swatches are three different colors corresponding to the colors used for the 2020, 2021, and 2022 column charts. The font is Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, or Calibri; the font size is 8 pt–12 pt; and the legend does not obscure the horizontal-axis title or sales-region labels. The legend is ordered 2020, 2021, and 2022 from left to right or from top to bottom, matching the column-series order.

+1: Trend chart axis lines: The horizontal axis, vertical axis, and depth axis are all dark-blue, black, or dark-gray single solid lines with a line width of 0.75 pt–1.25 pt. No axis line is missing, and the axis lines align with the tick-label positions.
-3: The trend chart data source does not reference the sales region, year, and shipment volume cell ranges in the workbook.
-1: The sales region, year, or sales amount data range in the data worksheet contains blanks, nonnumeric text in place of values, or an entire column of data in reversed order.
-1: The chart object covers the header of the source data range or covers more than 30% of the source data range.
